en: The Scripture on the Divine Incantation of the Eight Yangs of Heaven and Earth Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying in the Vast Mansion in the city of Vaiśālī. Ten...
As Fangxiang was thus surrounded by the fourfold assembly,
at that time the Bodhisattva Unobstructed rose from his seat amidst the great multitude and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

The sentient beings of this Jambudvīpa have been born in succession from one another since beginningless time, continuing without interruption; those with consciousness are few, while those without consciousness are many;
those who recite the Buddha’s name are few, while those who do not recite it are many;
those with supernormal powers are few, while those without them are many.
Those who uphold the precepts are few, while those who break them are many;
those who are diligent are few, while those who are indolent are many;
those who possess wisdom are few, while those who are ignorant and deluded are many.
Those with long lives are few, while those with short lifespans are many;
those who practice meditative concentration are few, while those who are distracted are many;
those who are wealthy and noble are few, while those who are poor and lowly are many.
Those who are gentle and flexible are few, while those who are harsh and stubborn are many;
those who practice generosity are few, while those who are stingy and greedy are many;
those who are sincere and truthful are few, while those who are deceitful and false are many.

Driven by the superficiality of worldly conventions and the bitter poison of official laws, the burdensome labor of corvée service oppresses the people; that the common folk suffer in such extreme poverty and find it so difficult to obtain their basic needs is entirely due to their belief in heterodoxy and their inverted views, which bring about such suffering.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will expound the Dharma of right view for the sake of sentient beings with wrong views, so that they may attain awakening and understanding,
and be liberated from all sufferings. The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent!"
"O Bodhisattva Unobstructed!
Your great compassion, in asking the Tathāgata about the Dharma of right view for the sake of sentient beings with false views, is inconceivable."
Listen attentively! Reflect upon this well!
I shall, for your sake, analyze and expound the Sūtra of the Eight Yangs of Heaven and Earth.
This sutra has been spoken by all Buddhas of the past, will be spoken by all Buddhas of the future, and is now being spoken by all Buddhas of the present.
Within the realm of heaven and earth, that which is most excellent and supreme among humans is more noble than all other things.
A human being (*puruṣa*) is truth and rectitude; their mind is free from falsehood and their bodily conduct is upright and true.
The left stroke (*zhuó*) represents truth, and the right stroke (*fú*) represents rectitude; because they constantly practice what is upright and true, they are called a human being.
Thus we know that a person can propagate the Way to nourish their own person; by relying on both the Way and the person, one accomplishes the holy path.
"Furthermore, Unobstructed Bodhisattva!

Although all sentient beings have obtained a human body, they are unable to cultivate merit. Turning their backs on the truth and heading toward the false, they create various kinds of evil karma. When their lives are about to end, they will inevitably sink into the sea of suffering and undergo various punishments."

If one hears this sutra and believes and accepts it without opposition, they shall immediately attain liberation from the perils of all sins and emerge from the ocean of suffering. Protected by benevolent deities, they will be free from all obstacles; their years will be extended and their life prolonged, such that no untimely death shall occur.
By the power of faith, one obtains such blessings—how much more so for those who are able to transcribe, uphold, read, and recite it in its entirety, practicing according to the Dharma?
The merit of such a person is ineffable and immeasurable, boundless and limitless; at the end of their lives, they shall all attain Buddhahood.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Unobstructed:

"If there are sentient beings who believe in heterodox and inverted views, they will immediately be plagued by demons, externalists, goblins, imps, the cries of birds, and a hundred strange monsters, as well as various malevolent ghosts and spirits, who will all vie to come and disturb them. These beings will be afflicted with calamitous illnesses, evil seeds, and malignant curses, enduring such suffering without respite."

If one encounters a virtuous friend who reads this sutra three times for them, all these malevolent ghosts will be completely extinguished; the illness will immediately be cured, and the body will become strong and full of vigor. Such is the merit and blessing obtained from the virtue of reading this sutra.

If there are sentient beings who abound in lust, anger, ignorance, stinginess, greed, or jealousy, and who upon seeing this sutra believe in, revere, and make offerings to it, and further recite it three times, then their ignorance and other evils will all be extinguished, and they shall attain a portion of the Buddha-dharma through loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
"Furthermore, Unobstructed Bodhisattva!

If good men or good women initiate any conditioned activity, they should first read this sutra three times before building walls, moving earth, or establishing a household—including southern and northern halls, eastern and western wings, kitchens, inner chambers, gates, wells, hearths, mortars and grinders, treasuries, and pens for domestic animals. Then, the daily and monthly deities, the Great General and the Tai-sui star, the Yellow Banner and the Leopard Tail, the five local earth spirits, the Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, and Black Tortoise, the prohibitions of the Six Jia, the twelve various gods, the Earth Chamber, the Subduing Dragon, and all malevolent ghosts and spirits will all hide away and retreat to the four quarters. Their shadows will vanish and they will be extinguished, not daring to cause harm; it shall be most greatly auspicious, and one will obtain immeasurable merit."

"Good son! After these meritorious works have been undertaken, the halls and dwellings will be eternally secure and the houses firm; wealth, honor, and prosperity will flourish, and what is not sought shall be obtained of itself.

If one travels afar or joins the military, or serves in office or engages in business, one will attain great success and profit. The family lineage will flourish with noble descendants, numbering a hundred sons and a thousand grandsons; fathers will be kind and sons filial, men loyal and women chaste; elder brothers will be respectful and younger brothers compliant, while husband and wife will live in harmony. With sincerity and righteousness, kinship will be deepened, and all that is wished for will be accomplished."
If there are sentient beings who are suddenly seized by government officials or dragged away by thieves and bandits, they shall obtain immediate liberation upon reading this sutra three times.

If there are good men or good women who receive, uphold, read, recite, or transcribe for others the *Eightfold Yang Sutra*, even if they enter fire or water, they shall not be burned or swept away; or if they are in mountains or marshes, tigers, wolves, and fierce beasts will keep their tracks and dare not approach, while benevolent deities will protect them until they achieve the Unsurpassed Way.

"If there be another person who frequently engages in false speech, frivolous speech, harsh speech, and double-tongued speech, yet is able to receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, they shall forever eliminate these four evil transgressions, attain the four kinds of unimpeded eloquence, and achieve the Buddha-way."

"If good sons or good daughters have parents who have committed offenses and are about to fall into hell to undergo immeasurable suffering on the day of their death, if those children recite this sutra seven times for them, the parents will immediately leave hell and be reborn in the heavens; there they shall see the Buddha, hear the Dharma, realize the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharmakṣānti*), and attain the path of Buddhahood."

The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Unobstructed: "During the time of Vipaśyin Buddha, there were laymen and laywomen who, though their minds lacked faith in heterodox views, revered and honored the Buddha-dharma. They transcribed this sutra, received, upheld, read, and recited it; whatever they undertook, they did immediately without asking any questions. Because of their right faith, they also practiced giving and made equal offerings. Consequently, they attained the untainted body and realized the path to Bodhi, becoming Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas named Universal Radiance (Puguang). The kalpa was called Great Leakage (Daleou), and the land was named Boundless (Wubian)."
"However, when people practice the bodhisattva path, they do so without grasping at any dharma; it is through the majestic power of this sutra that they obtain such a reward.
Furthermore, Unobstructed Bodhisattva!"

These eight *yáng* scriptures circulate throughout Jambudvīpa; wherever they may be, they are surrounded by eight bodhisattvas, various Brahma kings, and all enlightened spirits, who offer them incense and flowers as if they were no different from the Buddha himself.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Unobstructed, saying:

“If good sons and good daughters, for the sake of all sentient beings, expound this sutra, deeply penetrating the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*) and attaining its profound principle, they will immediately know the body and mind as the Buddha-body and the Dharma-mind; that by which they are able to know this is precisely wisdom.”

The eye constantly sees various inexhaustible forms; form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself form. Sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also empty—this is the Tathāgata of the Sublime Form-Body.
The ear constantly hears various inexhaustible sounds; sound is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself sound—this is the Tathāgata of Sublime Sound.
The nose constantly smells various inexhaustible fragrances; fragrance is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself fragrance—this is the Tathāgata of Fragrant Accumulation.
The tongue constantly perceives various inexhaustible flavors; flavor is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself flavor—this is the Tathāgata Dharma-Joy.
The body constantly experiences various inexhaustible tactile sensations; touch is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself touch—this is the Tathāgata Wisdom-Illumination.
The mind constantly thinks and is able to discern various inexhaustible phenomena; phenomena are themselves emptiness, and emptiness is itself phenomena—this is the Tathāgata Dharma-Illumination.
“Good son! Observe these six sense faculties as they manifest; everyone speaks of them constantly with empty mouths.
If one speaks virtuous words and the wholesome Dharma constantly turns within, one immediately accomplishes the Noble Path.”
If one speaks false words, evil dharmas will constantly revolve, and one will immediately fall into hell.
Good son! The principles of good and evil must be believed; they cannot be disregarded.

Good son! A person’s body and mind are the vessel for the Buddha-dharma, and they are also the twelve divisions of the great sūtras; since beginningless time, they have been read and recited without end, yet not even a hair’s breadth has been diminished.
The Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra and the mind of consciousness-only can be known by those who have seen their nature, but cannot be known by śrāvakas or ordinary worldlings. Good son!
If one reads and recites this sutra and deeply understands its true principle, one will immediately know that body and mind are the vessels for the Buddha-dharma.

If, however, one remains intoxicated and deluded without awakening, failing to realize that one's own mind is the very root of the Buddha-dharma, one will transmigrate through the various realms and fall into the evil paths, sinking forever into the ocean of suffering and never hearing even the name of the Buddha-dharma.

At that time, five hundred devaputras within the great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, attained the purity of the Dharma-eye; they were all greatly rejoiced and immediately resolved their minds upon the peerless, unsurpassed *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Bodhisattva Unobstructed again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
For people living in this world, birth and death are paramount; one does not choose the day of birth, for when the time arrives, one is born immediately."
Death does not choose its day; when the time arrives, one dies immediately.
For what reason do you inquire about auspicious hours and lucky days only at the point of enshrouding and burial?
Yet even after the enshrouding and burial, there remain further calamities: many fall into poverty, and few families do not suffer total extinction.

“I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain the causes and conditions for those sentient beings who hold wrong views and lack wisdom, so that they may attain the Right Path and eliminate their inversions.
The Buddha said, “Excellent, excellent!”
"Good sons! You are truly capable of inquiring about the matters of birth and death for sentient beings, as well as the rites of burial and interment.
Listen attentively!"
I shall now explain for you the principle of wisdom and the Dharma of the Great Way.
For the heavens and earth are vast and pure; the sun and moon are expansive and bright; and the seasons and years are excellent and beautiful—indeed, there is no difference between them.

"Good son! The Bodhisattva Human King possesses great compassion; he regards all sentient beings as his own infants. Descending to serve as a ruler of men, he acts as a parent to the common people. Conforming to worldly customs, he teaches worldly laws and creates the calendar to distribute throughout the world, so that they may know the seasons. It contains the designations for Ping, Man, Cheng, Shou, Kai, Bi, Jian, Chu, Ding, Zhi, Po, and Wei. Foolish people rely on these characters and place their trust in them, yet none can avoid their calamities and misfortunes."

Furthermore, they employ heterodox teachers to perform suppressive rites, claiming that this path is wrong; they vainly seek out false deities and prostrate before hungry ghosts, thereby repelling blessings and inviting calamity while suffering for themselves.

Such people turn their backs on the seasons of Heaven and oppose the principles of Earth; they flee from the radiance of the sun and moon to dwell in dark chambers, and they stray from the broad road of the Right Path to constantly seek out deviant tracks—how extreme is their perversion!

"Good son! If one recites this sutra three times at the time of childbirth, the child will be born easily; he will be exceedingly auspicious, intelligent, and wise, endowed with merit and virtue, and shall not meet an untimely death.
If one recites this sutra three times at the time of death, there will be no obstacles whatsoever, and one shall obtain immeasurable blessings."

"Good son! Every day is a great day, every month is a great month, and every year is a great year; there is truly no interval between them. However, as soon as the funeral arrangements are settled, one must immediately perform the burial."

On the day of the funeral rites, if one recites this sutra seven times, it will bring great good fortune and immeasurable blessings; the family will flourish, people will be honored, and longevity will be increased, such that at the time of death, all shall attain the Holy Path.
Good son! As for the site for burial, do not inquire whether it is east, west, south, or north; wherever it is secure and pleasing to all people, it will also be pleasing to the spirits and deities.

"If one recites this sutra three times and then performs the funeral rites, placing [the remains] within the tomb, there will forever be no calamities or obstacles; the family will become wealthy, prosperity will flourish, and there will be great good fortune.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"Auspicious day for conducting the funeral rites, A favorable time for interring the coffin. The burial is completed at a propitious hour; The deceased shall find rest and peace."
Reading and reciting the sutras throughout life and death brings immense benefit.
Every month is like a bright moon; every year is a most auspicious year.
To read the sutras at the time of funeral rites ensures that one’s glory will flourish for ten thousand generations.

At that time, seventy-seven thousand people among the assembly, having heard what the Buddha taught, had their minds opened and their intentions clarified; they abandoned the heterodox and returned to the orthodox, attained a portion of the Buddha-dharma, forever severed their doubts and delusions, and all resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Bodhisattva Unobstructed again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
All ordinary people regard marriage as a bond of kinship; they first inquire whether the match is suitable and subsequently select an auspicious day before finally consummating the union."
After entering into marriage, those who enjoy wealth and status and grow old together are few, while those who suffer poverty and endure separation in life or parting in death are many.
Given that both groups equally believe in heterodoxy, how can such a disparity exist?
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will resolve the doubts of the assembly. The Buddha said, "Good son!
Listen attentively!
I shall explain it for you.
Heaven is yang and earth is yin; the moon is yin and the sun is yang; water is yin and fire is yang; the female is yin and the male is yang.
When the qi of heaven and earth unite, all grasses and trees grow;
when the sun and moon interact, the four seasons and eight nodes become manifest;
when water and fire succeed one another, all myriad things ripen.
When men and women are in harmonious accord, descendants flourish;
this is the constant way of Heaven, the natural principle, and the law of worldly truth.
O son of good family!

Foolish people lack wisdom; they place their trust in false teachers who practice divination in hopes of fortune, yet fail to cultivate goodness and instead commit various evil deeds. After their lives end, those who again obtain a human body are as rare as the dust upon a fingernail, while those who fall into the hells or become animals or hungry ghosts are as numerous as the soil of the great earth.

Good son! Those who have obtained a human body, possess right faith, and cultivate goodness are like the soil on a fingernail; those who believe in heterodoxy and commit evil deeds are like the soil of the great earth.

"Good son! When desiring to form a marriage alliance, one should not inquire whether there is mutual conflict between the elements of water and fire, whether there is mutual aversion between the fetal membranes, or whether their ages are incompatible; one should simply consult the books of destiny and fortune to know the extent of their merit and virtue before taking them as kinsmen."

On the day of the wedding reception, one should recite this sutra three times to complete the ceremony; this is the principle of virtue begetting virtue and brightness following brightness. Thus, the family will be exalted and noble, with descendants flourishing and thriving; they shall possess intelligence and wisdom, and filial piety and respect will be passed down through generations. This shall bring great good fortune and prosperity, free from premature death, as they become fully endowed with merit and virtue, all attaining the Way of the Buddha.

At that time, there were eight bodhisattvas who, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, attained great dhāraṇīs; they constantly dwelt among human beings, blending their light with the mundane dust while refuting the heterodox and establishing the orthodox.
Their names were:
the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla, free from outflows; the Bodhisattva Ratnākara, free from outflows;
the Bodhisattva Guhagupta, free from outflows; and the Bodhisattva Naradatta, free from outflows.
The Bodhisattva Sumerugambhīra attained the harmony of the exhaustion of outflows; the Bodhisattva Indradatta attained the harmony of the exhaustion of outflows;
the Bodhisattva Saṃtaraṇa attained the harmony of the exhaustion of outflows; and the Bodhisattva Nairātmyadarśin attained the harmony of the exhaustion of outflows.
These eight bodhisattvas together addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We have received and maintained the divine dhāraṇī spells from the various Buddhas and now speak them. May they protect those who receive, maintain, read, and recite the *Eight Yang* Sūtra so that they shall forever be free from fear, and cause all unwholesome beings to be unable to harm or obstruct the Dharma masters who recite this sūtra.”
He then spoke this mantra before the Buddha:
“Akhaṇi (1) ni-akhaṇi (2) abhira (3) mandre (4) mandrare (5) svāhā.”
“World-Honored One!

If there should be any unwholesome ones who wish to come and harass the Dharma Master, upon hearing me recite this mantra, their heads shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Anantagātra rose from his seat, approached the Buddha, and said to him:
"World-Honored One,
why is this called the Sūtra of the Eight Auspiciousnesses?"

I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain its meaning for the sake of the assembly, enabling them to attain awakening, swiftly reach their original mind, enter the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, and forever sever doubt and regret.
The Buddha said: “Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!”
Listen attentively! I shall now explain it for you. Regarding the *Eightfold Yang Scripture*:

"Eight" (*ba*) signifies differentiation; "Yang" (*yang*) signifies clear understanding. It refers to clearly understanding the principle of the Great Vehicle’s emptiness and non-substantiality, and being able to fully differentiate that the causes and conditions of the eight consciousnesses are empty and unattainable.
Why are the eight consciousnesses called the "lengthwise threads" (*dīrgha-sūtra*) and the eight *yáng* called the "crosswise threads" (*tiryak-sūtra*)?
Because the lengthwise and crosswise threads intersect to form the scriptural teachings, it is named the *Bāyáng jīng*.
What are the "eight"? They are the eight consciousnesses; why are they called the eight consciousnesses?

The eye is the consciousness of form; the ear is the consciousness of sound; the nose is the consciousness of fragrance; the tongue is the consciousness of taste; the body is the consciousness of touch; and the mind is the consciousness of discernment.
The six sense organs are the six consciousnesses; together with the *ālayavijñāna* and the *saṃtānavijñāna*, these are called the eight consciousnesses.

When one clearly discerns that the source of these eight consciousnesses is empty and ungraspable, one immediately knows that the two eyes are the Heaven of Radiant Light (*Ābhāsvara-deva*), and within this Heaven of Radiant Light appears the World-Honored One of Sun and Moon Radiance;
the two ears are the Heaven of Sound-Hearers (*Śrāvaka-deva*), and within this Heaven of Sound-Hearers appears the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Sound.
The two nostrils are the Heaven of Buddha-Fragrance; within the Heaven of Buddha-Fragrance appears the Tathāgata Fragrant Accumulation.
The mouth is the Heaven of Dharma-Flavor; within the Heaven of Dharma-Flavor appears the Tathāgata Dharma-Joy.
The body is the Heaven of Vairocana; within the Heaven of Vairocana appear the Buddha Accomplished-Vairocana, the Buddha Mirror-Image-Vairocana, and the Buddha Radiance-Vairocana.
The mind is the Heaven of Non-conceptuality; within the Heaven of Non-conceptuality, there appears the Tathāgata Immovable and the Buddha Great Radiance.
The heart is the Heaven of the Dharma-realm; within the Heaven of the Dharma-realm, there appears the Tathāgata King of Emptiness.
The Ālayavijñāna Deva expounded the *Āgama Sūtras* and the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*;
the Ālayavijñāna Deva expounded the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* and the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*.
"Good son! The Buddha is the Dharma, and the Dharma is the Buddha; when united as a single mark, they manifest as the Tathāgata Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū.

When the Buddha spoke this sutra, the entire great earth shook in six ways, and light illuminated heaven and earth without limit. It was vast and boundless beyond naming; all darkness became bright and clear, all hells were simultaneously extinguished, and all offenders were freed from suffering, each vowing to attain unexcelled bodhicitta.

At that time, within the great assembly, eighty-eight thousand bodhisattvas simultaneously attained buddhahood, becoming Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas known as Emptiness-King (Kongwang). The kalpa was named Free from Suffering (Liku), and their lands were named Boundless (Wubian).
All the people practiced the six pāramitās of the bodhisattvas and attained the dharma of non-attainment.
Sixty-six thousand bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās attained great dhāraṇī and entered the gate of non-duality.
Countless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans attained the purity of the Dharma-eye and practiced the bodhisattva path.
"Furthermore, good son!

If there is anyone who, on the day they receive office and ascend to their position, or at the time of entering a new residence, briefly reads this sutra three times, it will bring great auspiciousness and prosperity; benevolent deities will provide protection, extending their years and increasing their lifespan, such that merit and virtue become complete."
"Good son! If one reads this sutra once, it is as if one has read an entire collection of all the sutras;
if one transcribes one fascicle of it, it is as if one has transcribed an entire collection of all the sutras."
Their merit is incalculable and immeasurable, equal to space and without limit; such persons as these shall achieve the Noble Path.
"Furthermore, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Anantakāya!

If there are sentient beings who do not believe in the True Dharma and constantly give rise to wrong views, and upon suddenly hearing this sutra they immediately slander it, saying it was not spoken by the Buddha—such persons will, in their present life, contract leprosy; foul sores and pus and blood will flow all over their bodies, and because of their rank stench and filth, everyone will loathe and despise them. On the day their lives end, they will immediately fall into the Avīci Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering. Flames from above penetrate below and flames from below penetrate above; iron spears and iron forks pierce through every part of their bodies. Molten copper is poured into their mouths, rotting their sinews and bones. Day and night, they die ten thousand deaths and undergo ten thousand births, enduring great agony without any rest.
"Because of slandering this sutra, one incurs such offenses.
For the sake of these offenders, the Buddha spoke in verse:
"The body is a natural body; The five limbs are naturally complete."
Longevity is naturally long; old age is naturally old;
birth is naturally born; death is naturally dead.
Seeking longevity, one does not find it; seeking brevity, one does not find it.
Suffering and joy you shall experience for yourself; whether you follow the wrong or the right path depends upon you alone.
If you wish to perform meritorious deeds in the conditioned world, read the scriptures without questioning a teacher.
Through thousands, tens of thousands, and millions of lifetimes, you shall attain the Way and turn the Wheel of Dharma.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the entire great assembly attained what they had never experienced before; their minds became clear and their intentions pure, and they leaped for joy. All beheld that all marks are non-marks, entering the Buddha’s knowledge and vision and awakening to the Buddha’s knowledge and vision—yet there was no entering and no awakening, no knowing and no seeing, for by not grasping even a single dharma, they attained the bliss of nirvana.
All these bodhisattvas, noble assemblies, celestial deities, and terrestrial spirits were filled with joy and reverently practiced it.
The *Sūtra on the Divine Incantation of the Eight Yangs of Heaven and Earth* spoken by the Buddha is hereby concluded.
